title: What to Assess Before Automating a Company With Multiple Branches
summary: See what to consider before automating processes in companies with multiple branches, franchises, or holdings.
body_markdown:
Before automating a company with multiple branches, you need to map which processes are the same across every unit and which vary by branch, franchise, or cost center, plus decide whether each unit will have its own ERP account or a shared structure. Without this mapping, automation built for headquarters can break when applied to another unit with different rules.


This is a common problem in chains, franchises, and holdings: each branch grew solving its own problems its own way, with spreadsheets and processes that differ slightly from one another. When the company tries to standardize, it finds out "the same process" actually has small variations in each location.


Ignoring these differences when automating creates rework: approvals that don't respect the right threshold per branch, entries posted to the wrong ERP account, or inventory that doesn't reflect the real transfer between units.


## What Usually Varies Between Branches


- Approval threshold by amount and by unit
- Cost center and internal code for each branch
- Fiscal or operational rules specific to a region
- Number of connected ERP accounts (one per company ID or a central one)
- Level of autonomy each local manager has over the process


## What to Evaluate Before Standardizing the Automation


- Whether the process really needs to be identical or just follow the same general pattern
- How inventory or data transfer between branches will be automated
- Whether the platform supports multiple company IDs with no extra cost per connected account
- Who will have permission to adjust the process at each unit
- How each branch will see the flow (dynamic connected field or fixed option)


## Best Practices for Scaling Automation Across Units


- Build a base process and allow small, controlled variations per branch
- Centralize the execution log for automations, even across several ERP accounts
- Assign a single owner for governance of automations across units
- Test the automation at one pilot branch before rolling it out to all of them
